import sys
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print("Usage: python arxiv_search.py <query> <N>", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    query = sys.argv[1]
    N = int(sys.argv[2])
    encoded_query = urllib.parse.quote(query)

    url = f"http://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:{encoded_query}&max_results={N}"
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response:
            if response.getcode() != 200:
                print("No results found", file=sys.stderr)
                sys.exit(1)
            xml_data = response.read().decode('utf-8')
    except urllib.error.URLError as e:
        print("No results found", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    root = ET.fromstring(xml_data)
    entries = root.findall(".//entry")

    if not entries:
        print("No results found", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    for entry in entries:
        title = entry.find("title").text
        authors = []
        for author in entry.findall("author/name"):
            authors.append(author.text)
        print(f"Title: {title}")
        print(f"Authors: {', '.join(authors)}\n")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
events.reasoning: The script fails to handle the Atom XML namespace used by the arXiv API. The API returns elements in the default namespace `http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom`, so ElementTree tag names are like `{http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom}entry`, `{http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom}title`, and `{http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom}name`. The code searches for unqualified tags such as `.//entry`, `title`, and `author/name`, which will not match. As a result, `entries` will be empty even when the response contains valid entries, and the script will always print `No results found` to stderr and exit 1 instead of printing titles and authors.
